title: NFL wind under on observed wind, since 1999
result: The under won 57.2% against the close in games with observed wind of 15 mph or more (+9% at −110).
note: Observed wind at kickoff, not the forecast the rule bets on.

title: NFL wind under on observed wind, 2024–26
result: The rule went 18–18 on observed wind in 2024–26.
note: Listed in the playbook as evidence against.

title: NFL wind under on 1-day forecasts
note: Listed in the playbook as evidence against.

title: NFL wind under, replayed on NWS MOS forecasts as issued (2004–25)
result: On the forecasts as they were issued, NFL Rule B went 337–261–9 (56.4%) on 607 signals, ROI +7.6% at an assumed −110; it is far from this project's bar and is not an independent test.
note: 333 of the 607 signals are games the observed-wind evidence already counts; the 274 only the forecast flagged went 148–122–4 (54.8%, p = 0.23). In 2007–21, the 15 seasons with a second source of lines, it went 214–181–5 (54.2%, 400 signals, p = 0.25).

title: College football wind under on observed wind, 2006–25
result: The under won 56.6% against the close in games with observed wind of 15 mph or more (+8% at −110); 57.4% in 2016–25 and 56.4% in 2021–25.
note: Uses observed airport-station weather, not forecasts. No p-value is written for it, so it is not counted as clearing the bar.

title: College football wind under against the opening total
result: The under won 60.9% against the opener, with totals falling 1.4 points by kickoff.
note: Observed wind. No p-value is written for it, so it is not counted as clearing the bar.

title: College football wind under, replayed on the forecasts available at bet time (2024–25)
result: On the forecasts that existed at bet time the rule went 61–46–3 (57.0%) at the close, ROI +8.8% at −110; two seasons can't confirm it.
bar: 0.05 split over 135 variants (this replay made the count 135)
note: Every entry is at the closing total at −110, so the price gates could not bind.

title: College football wind under, replayed on NWS MOS forecasts as issued (2006–25)
result: On the forecasts as they were issued, the rule went 715–555–14 (56.3%) on 1,284 signals over 20 seasons, a return of +7.5% per bet at an assumed −110; it beats break-even by ordinary standards but does not clear this project's bar.
note: Not an independent test: 602 of the 1,284 signals are games the observed-wind evidence already counts, and the 682 games only the forecast flagged went 365–311–6 (54.0%), p = 0.21.

title: College football wind under, replayed on NWS MOS forecasts as issued (FBS 2023–25)
result: On forecasts as issued the rule went 112–86–2 (56.6%) at the close, ROI +8.0% at −110; not evidence of an edge on its own.
note: 95% interval for the win rate: 49.6–63.3%. This was the method check; the full 2006–25 run is the entry above, and includes these seasons.

title: College football high totals go under (Rule HT), 2016–25
result: When the closing total was at least the prior season's mean + 10, the under went 373–273 (57.7%), above 50% in 9 of 10 seasons.
note: The era split was chosen after looking (2006–15 was 48.2%).

title: Rule HT restated on the corrected spread data (#36)
result: On the corrected spread data the pre-check's by-spread split sums to 502–393 (56.1%), or 434–326 (57.1%) on FBS-involved games.
note: The rule, threshold and forward test are as registered; the history is restated on more games. No p-value is written for it.

title: Key-number table against the registered pricing model
result: The table did not beat the registered pricing model on any of the 8 comparisons declared before the run, so the pricing model stays as registered.

title: College football: where games land next to a half-point line
result: The table's log loss is 1.5% lower out of sample (95% interval 0.7% to 2.1%; better in 15 of 20 seasons).
note: Found after the first run, so a lead for 2027, not a result. n is half-point closes.

title: NFL: games landing on a whole-number closing total
result: Since 2015, when the closing total is a whole number, the game lands on it only 1.9% of the time, against 3.5% in 1999–2014.
note: Found after the first run; SBR's closes show the same drop (p = 0.03).

title: Today's paper-to-money gate
result: “Paper until 20 settled signals show positive average CLV” passes 49–51% of the time with no edge at all, so it isn't a filter.
n: 40,000 simulated runs of 40 signals per case
bar: Not a betting test: it adds no variants
note: A simulation of a staking rule, not evidence about any bet.

title: The recommended sequential gate (not chosen yet)
result: With no edge it passes on CFB about 2.6% of the time (4–5% if signals cluster as much as the most pessimistic estimate); real money this season about 21% of the time at half the historical line move, 65% at the full move.
n: 40,000 simulated runs of 40 signals per case
bar: Not a betting test: it adds no variants
note: The choice of gate is the owner's; until then both STRATEGY.md files stand as written.

title: The keep test passes too often
result: Signals move together, so the keep test as first registered (the plain interval) passes a no-edge rule about 5.5% of the time on CFB instead of 2.7%, and 8–10% on NFL instead of 2%.
n: 40,000 simulated runs of 40 signals per case
bar: Not a betting test: it adds no variants
note: nfl-weather amendment 7 and cfb-weather amendment 5 (Sep 29) register the wider of the plain interval and one grouped by game day. In the realistic case it keeps a no-edge rule 2.8 to 3.0% of the time on CFB and 5.8 to 7.4% on NFL, against an intended 2.5%. It is registered for both sports as an improvement, with its remaining error stated in the amendments.
